relation_to_odsp.role: biological follow-up motivated by the N2 morphology-to-island reversal

ecological_question: Across neighboring Palmer Archipelago islands, is apparent penguin trait differentiation generated mainly by species turnover, or does a persistent within-species island phenotype remain after restricting to Adelie penguins?

hypotheses.statement: Archipelago-scale morphology-to-island predictability is dominated by species composition rather than persistent within-species island morphology.
hypotheses.evidence: frozen N2 pooled versus species-conditioned score decomposition

hypotheses.statement: If islands maintain persistent Adelie phenotypes, island main effects should improve fit after sex, year, laying date and clutch completion are controlled.
If within-species island states are temporally labile, island-by-year terms should outperform a fixed-island model and island rankings should reverse among years.
A persistent island phenotype should allow island identity learned from two years to classify held-out-year Adelie individuals above the one-third balanced-accuracy reference.

transfer_test.preprocessing: training-fold sex residualization and training SD scaling

interpretation_boundaries: Do not claim local adaptation from this observational dataset.
Do not interpret island-by-year structural differences as individual plasticity; different adults were sampled.
Body mass is a condition-sensitive trait measured during egg laying.
Blood stable isotopes integrate pre-breeding foraging over prior weeks and are not local-island foraging measurements.
Three years and three islands are a short, small replication window; long-term PAL-LTER data are needed for environmental mechanism tests.
